The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 07122018 at about 8.00 am., when the Petitioner was proceeding in a Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA05HL 8804 on left side Road and reached near Kallukombari gate, Nagamangala to Bindiganavele Road, Mandya District, at that time, driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA11F0044 which was going in front of the Petitioner's vehicle in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life without observing traffic rules and regulations and without indicator and hand signal immediately took right and suddenly applied SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2929/2019 the brake and thereby the back side body of the bus dashed against the Petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to which the Petitioner fell down and sustained fatal injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to near by Government hospital,
Nagamangala, wherein, first aid treatment was given and thereafter, he shifted to AIMS hospital at B.G.Nagar and thereafter, he was admitted in Sparsha hospital at Bangalore, wherein, the Petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 07122018 to 19 122018.
The Petitioner had spent Rs.5,00,000/ towards medical treatment, conveyance and nourishment charges.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as a Driver and earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving and applying the break without signal by the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA 11F0044.
The Respondent is the owner cum internal insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2929/2019 Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

5. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondent, it appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed Written Statement interalia denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the said accident and also the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioner.

Further it denied that, the said accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA11F 0044 and contended that, the said accident was occurred due to negligence of the Petitioner himself and therefore it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, Respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

6. On the rival Pleadings my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
 SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2929/2019  ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries due to RTA alleged to have been occurred on 07122018 at about 8.00 a.m. near Kalkombari gate, Nagamangala to Bindiganavele A.R.Kumar vs The Managing Director on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100497755/
2 Road, Nagamangala town, Mandya district, due to the rash and negligent driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA11F0044 ?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

He has denied the suggestions put to him in his crossexamination.

18. The Learned counsel for Respondent has taken contention that, there was a bus stop in the accident spot and therefore the offending bus moved in slow manner to pick the students who are waiting for bus in the said bus stand.
19. In this regard the Respondent has examined its Driver by name K. Venkatesh as RW.1.
RW.1 has reiterated the Objection Statement contentions in his chiefaffidavit.
In the crossexamination he admitted that the FIR was registered against him and the said criminal case is pending for trial.
Further he deposed that he has not challenged the Charge sheet.

Hence, the tribunal can draw inference that the said accident has occurred by the RW.1 due to his rash and negligent driving and without indicator and hand signal, he took the bus to the right side and suddenly applied the brake.

Further the sketch shown in the Mahazar also does not exhibit the Bus stop situated near the accident spot.
Hence, the evidence of the RW.1 that after giving signal he stopped the bus in order to facilitate the passengers and school students to board the bus is not believable.

21. Moreover, though the PW.1 and 3 subjected for cross examination by the Learned Counsel for Respondent, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve their testimony in respect of the accident caused by the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 22. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA11F0044 by its driver and due to the accident the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
23. Issue No.2 : As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending KSRTC Bus by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
24. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 38 years.
Further, the Petitioner has produced his DL i.e., Ex.P 8, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2929/2019 05.06.1980.
The accident has taken place on 07.12.2018.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 38 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
25. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was working as a Driver and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of actual income proof, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since, the accident has occurred in the year 2018, the income of the petitioner is notionally taken at Rs.12,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
26. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2929/2019 I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
27.
It is stated in the petition that, in the accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P5 issued by the Medical Officer of the Sparsh hospital shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained the following injuries i.e.,
1) Severe head injury 2) Right temporal fracture EDH+ FTP accute SDH with mass effect and midline shaft 3) Multiple facial bone fractures 4) Right Traumatic optic neuro injury 28.
As per the opinion of the doctor, the said injuries are grievous in nature.

A.R.Kumar vs The Managing Director on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100497755/
7 29.
PW2 Dr.Abhinandan has also reiterated the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the Road Traffic Accident and also treatment given to the Petitioner.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
31.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.75,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:

32. The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he has taken the treatment at Sparsha hospital,
Bengaluru and AIMS Hospital, Bengaluru.

Upon going through Ex.P.7  Discharge summary of Sparsha hospital, Bengaluru shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2929/2019 from 07.12.2018 to 19.12.2018.
Another Discharge Summary of Sparsha Hospital shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 1303 2019 to 16032019.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 17 days.
33. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as three months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.37,500/ under this head (@ Rs.12,500/ per month ).

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
34.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.9,000/ (@ Rs.100/ per day) towards attendants charges, Rs.9,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.9,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.27,000/ under this head.

V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
35.
The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent more than 8,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.

In order to prove this fact, he has produced total hospital and Medical A.R.Kumar vs The Managing Director on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100497755/
8 bills, which is marked at Ex.P.9 and Prescriptions at Ex.P.11.
I have gone through the said Medical bills.
The bill at Sl.No.33 is Ambulance bill.
The PW.1 has also produced Ex.P13 Medical bills.
Therefore, the total acceptable medical bills comes to Rs.6,42,520/.
Hence, by rounding of the same, the same to be taken at Rs.6,42,600/. Hence, I am SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2929/2019 of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,42,600/ under this head.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
36.
The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

37. Further, the Petitioner got examined witness by name Dr.Abhinandan J.G. as P.W.2 through Court Commissioner who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by the Petitioner and he assessed the Neurological disability at 40%.
Further PW2 got marked 5 documents at ExP13 to ExP17.
The Court Commissioner has also filed his report along with the evidence recorded by him along with SCCH 15 21 MVC No.2929/2019 proceedings.
ExP13 is the two Inpatient files.
ExP14 is the OPD file.
Ex P15 is the MRI film with Report.
ExP16 is the Neuropsychological Evaluation Report prepared by Dr.Kumaraswamy D.R.
ExP17 is the VEP report.
38. In the crossexamination PW2 has deposed that he has personally treated the Petitioner and he is one among the team of Doctor who gave treatment to the Petitioner.
Further he admitted that ExP16 is not prepared by him.
Further, PW.2 admitted that the Petitioner was discharged in stable condition.
Further he admitted that the Petitioner can do his daily activities without any interference, but with difficulties he can manage.

39. It is pertinent to note here that upon going through ExP16 i.e., is the Neuro psychological report which was prepared by one Dr.Kumaraswamy D.R. and he assessed SCCH 15 22 MVC No.2929/2019 Cognitive disability at 50%.

The petitioner has not examined the said Dr.
Kumaraswamy who has assessed his cognitive disability.
Further, PW.1 is subjected for cross examination and he answered to all the questions posed to him.

Therefore, by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 15% would be just and proper.
40. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 15.

With multiplier of 15, income of Rs.12,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at xx%, the loss of future income comes to  3,37,500/ (Rs.12,500/ x 12 =
1,50,000/, Rs.1,50,000/x 15 x15/100 = 3,37,500/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 3,37,500/ under this head.

9  TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE  PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
41.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs.1,00,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 75,000/
3. Loss of income during the Rs. 37,500/ laid up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 27,000/ diet, and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses Rs.6,42,600/
6. Loss of Future Income Rs.3,37,500/ Total Rs.12,19,600/
42.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.12,19,600/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending K.S.R.T.C. bus bearing Reg.No.KA11F0044.
In this case, the Respondent is the R.C. Owner cum Internal Insurer of K.S.R.T.C. bus.
Therefore, the Respondent has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
44. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.12,19,600/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from SCCH 15 25 MVC No.2929/2019 the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner and directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
